name: Zscaler
scope_notes: Covers Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA, OneAPI via Authentication Service / ZIdentity). SaaS; OneAPI needs services linked to Authentication Service; legacy ZIA API needs an API subscription; Workflow Automation, Client Connector and ZDX API keys not covered.

controls.name: API client Status (enable/disable)
controls.what: A disabled client cannot get tokens, and its issued tokens are revoked.

controls.name: Delete API client
controls.what: Deleting a client revokes its tokens.

controls.name: Revoke access token
controls.what: Revoke a single active token by Client ID or JTI.

controls.name: Access Token Validity
controls.what: Sets token lifetime from 1 minute to 24 hours.
controls.setting: Add/Edit API Client > Access Token Validity

controls.name: API resources (scope)
controls.what: Client gets one API role per Zscaler service.

controls.name: API Client Access Policy
controls.what: Allow/Block rules by API resource and time window, one rule per client.
controls.setting: Administration > API > API Client Access Policy

controls.name: Delete / regenerate / edit Cloud Service API Key
controls.what: Any of these immediately invalidates the old key.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > Cloud Service API Key

controls.name: Admin role functional scope
controls.what: Key access is given only to admins with functional scope for API services.

controls.name: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server status / delete
controls.what: Disable or delete a trusted external authorization server.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > OAuth 2.0 Authorization Servers

controls.name: Required JWT claims (audience, issuer, client ID)
controls.what: Mandate claim checks on external tokens.

controls.name: API Roles
controls.what: Per-category Full/View Only/None permissions; cannot modify admins.
controls.setting: Administration > Role Management > Internet & SaaS > Add API Role

controls.name: ZPA API key Status
controls.setting: Administration > API > Private Access API > Edit

controls.name: ZPA API key Role
controls.what: Predefined or custom role (e.g. API Read Only) enforces RBAC on ZPA API operations.

controls.name: Session Validity Interval
controls.setting: Add API Keys > Session Validity Interval

controls.name: Regenerate / delete Sandbox API token
controls.what: Regenerating immediately invalidates the old token.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > Sandbox API Token

controls.name: Delete the API key
controls.what: Deleting the organization's only Cloud Service API key stops all legacy ZIA API requests until a new key is added.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > Cloud Service API Key > Delete

controls.name: Delete the API token
controls.what: Deleting the Sandbox API tokens stops Sandbox Submission API requests.
controls.setting: Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > Sandbox API Token > Delete

no_control.what: Admins provisioned through a third-party IdP cannot use the legacy ZIA API, so this path needs a password admin hosted in Authentication Service outside IdP SSO.

controls_unknown: Source-IP restriction for OneAPI clients, ZPA keys or legacy ZIA sessions (Admin Sign-On Policy and ZIA restricted admin access pages do not state API coverage)
Whether the Authentication Service Admin Sign-On Policy or MFA applies to legacy ZIA API password logins
Whether deleting/disabling a ZPA API key or ZIA authorization server ends already-issued bearer tokens
Whether API client create/delete and token revoke appear as named actions in Authentication Service audit logs (documented actions are generic Create/Update/Delete)
Whether read-only (GET) API calls are recorded in any audit log
Expiry of JWT key pairs (zscaler-2) and Sandbox tokens
OneAPI rate limits (only legacy limits fetched)

authentication.summary: An API client in Authentication Service (ZIdentity) uses the OAuth 2.0 client credentials grant with a client ID and secret at <tenant>.zslogin.net/oauth2/v1/token (audience https://api.zscaler.com) and gets a JWT access token for OneAPI.

federation.details: Docs do not describe workload/OIDC federation for secret-based clients.

ip_restriction.boundary: API Client Access Policy criteria are time and API resources only; no source-IP criterion is documented. Whether the Admin Sign-On Policy applies to API clients is not stated.

lifetime.summary: Secret 30-365 days; access token 1 min-24 h

renewal.expiry_basis: Access token validity set per client (1 min-24 h); secret has its own 30-365 day validity
renewal.summary: Request a new token with the secret; rotate by adding a second secret (max two; a third replaces the most recent).

administration.summary: Admins with API Clients & Resources permission create, edit, enable/disable, delete clients and revoke tokens. Scope is one API resource (role) per Zscaler service.
administration.conditions: Zscaler services must be linked to Authentication Service; up to 256 API clients per tenant.

offboard.details: An API client represents an application or service, not a user.

inventory.details: API Clients page (Administration > API > API Clients) lists all clients and exports CSV; issued tokens on Administration > API > Tokens.

token_format.notes: JWT access token (bearer); client ID auto-generated.

log_sources.name: Authentication Service Issued Tokens page
log_sources.notes: Administration > API > Tokens; lists Client ID, JTI, issued/expires, status.

log_sources.name: Authentication Service audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Authentication Service; Interface field shows API-based; stream to SIEM via NSS (auditlogtype ZID).

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

log_sources.name: ZPA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Records admin and API actions; Client ID column; 6-month retention.

Created by OneAPI; visible when Authentication Service enabled

anomaly_cues: Tokens issued for a client outside its normal schedule (Issued At filter)

New secret added to an existing client

containment.steps: Disable or delete the API client (revokes its tokens), or revoke individual tokens on the Tokens page; remove secrets/keys.
containment.notes: Revoked tokens can no longer be used; disabling the client revokes its tokens.

unknown: Exact audit event name for API client and token actions
Whether token issuance is itself audited
Whether OneAPI GET calls are logged

credentials.name: OneAPI API client (JWKS URL or certificate/public key)

authentication.summary: Same API client type, but the client signs a JWT with its private key; Authentication Service verifies it using a hosted JWKS URL or an uploaded .pem public key, then issues an access token.

federation.details: Keys can be served from a customer-hosted JWKS URL, but no workload identity federation (e.g. cloud OIDC tokens) is documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: Same as zscaler-1: no IP criterion documented in API Client Access Policy.

lifetime.summary: Key pair has no documented expiry; access token 1 min-24 h

renewal.summary: Client signs a new JWT assertion to get a new token; key rotation via JWKS URL or new .pem.

administration.summary: Managed on the same API Clients page as zscaler-1.

offboard.details: An API client represents an application or service, not a user.

inventory.details: API Clients page (Administration > API > API Clients); issued tokens on Administration > API > Tokens.

token_format.notes: JWT access token; client authenticates with signed JWT assertion.

credentials.name: Cloud Service API Key with ZIA admin credentials (legacy ZIA API)

authentication.summary: Legacy ZIA API: POST /api/v1/authenticatedSession with admin username, password, an obfuscated 12-character org API key and timestamp; returns a JSESSIONID cookie.

federation.details: Password-based; in Authentication Service tenants, users provisioned via third-party IdPs cannot authenticate to the APIs.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP restriction for API sessions is documented on the API pages fetched.

lifetime.summary: Org key never expires; session cookie expires in 5 minutes by default

renewal.summary: Re-POST /authenticatedSession with the same key and password.

administration.summary: One key per org, provisioned by Zscaler with an API subscription. Admins with the needed role can edit, regenerate or delete it; access is also limited by the admin's role.
administration.conditions: Requires API subscription; Zscaler may disable the key for abuse.

sso.details: API login uses a username and password for an admin hosted on Authentication Service; IdP-provisioned admins cannot use the API, so IdP SSO is not in the path.

inventory.details: One key per organization, shown on the Cloud Service API Key page.

token_format.notes: 12-character alphanumeric org key, sent obfuscated with a timestamp; session is a JSESSIONID cookie.

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

credential_id_fields.notes: Admin login used with the key

anomaly_cues: Sign In with Interface API from an unexpected IP
Key regenerate/edit by an unexpected admin

containment.steps: Regenerate, edit or delete the Cloud Service API Key; reset or remove the admin account used.
containment.notes: Docs: deleting the key ensures no further API requests are possible; old key invalidated immediately.

unknown: Whether an existing JSESSIONID survives key deletion for its remaining minutes

calls.log_notes: ZIA audit Sign In action; Interface API
Audit logs record actions; GETs not confirmed

calls.reveals: URL categories (up to 100 URLs per request)

credentials.name: ZIA OAuth 2.0 with external authorization server (PingFederate, Okta, Entra ID)

authentication.summary: A client app registered in the customer's IdP gets a client-credentials JWT with scope <cloud>::<orgid>::<API role>; ZIA validates the signature via the server's JWKS and the scope claim.

federation.details: ZIA trusts tokens issued by the customer's PingFederate, Okta or Entra ID; audience, issuer and client ID claims can be required.

ip_restriction.boundary: Not documented on the ZIA side; any IP policy would be the external IdP's.

lifetime.summary: Token lifetime set in the external OAuth service

renewal.summary: Client requests a new token from its IdP.

administration.summary: Admins add, edit, enable/disable or delete authorization servers; API roles (up to 16, rank 7, cannot modify admins) set what the client can do.
administration.conditions: Requires API subscription and API roles; cloud service API only.

offboard.details: Client-credentials grant works outside the context of users.

inventory.details: Zscaler lists configured authorization servers; the individual OAuth clients live in the external IdP.

inventory.ui: ZIA Admin Portal > Administration > Cloud Service API Security > OAuth 2.0 Authorization Servers tab (servers only; list OAuth clients in the external IdP)

expiry.ui: Set in the external OAuth service, e.g. Okta: authorization server > Access Policies > rule > Access token lifetime is. Check expires_in in the token response

token_format.notes: JWT issued by the customer's IdP.

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

anomaly_cues: API changes by oauth-<role> user from unknown IPs

containment.steps: Disable or delete the authorization server in ZIA; disable the client in the IdP; tighten the API role.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether ZIA rejects already-issued, unexpired JWTs after IdP-side revocation.

unknown: Effect of disabling the server on live tokens
Which IdP client made a call (only role user is logged)

calls.log_notes: Audit logs record actions; GETs not confirmed

calls.reveals: URL categories (up to 100 URLs per request)

credentials.name: ZPA API key (client ID and client secret, legacy ZPA API)

authentication.summary: ZPA API key = client ID + secret, posted to https://config.private.zscaler.com/signin to get a bearer token for /mgmtconfig endpoints.

ip_restriction.boundary: Not documented for ZPA API keys.

lifetime.summary: Key itself has no documented expiry; session validity up to 3,600 s

renewal.summary: Call /signin again with the same client ID and secret.

administration.summary: Admins with full API Key Management access create keys with a status and RBAC role (e.g. API Read Only); keys can be edited, disabled or deleted. Authentication Service keys show read-only here.
administration.conditions: Keys created via Zscaler Deception cannot be edited or deleted here.

offboard.details: The key carries its own API role and is not tied to an admin user.

inventory.details: API Keys page (Administration > API > Private Access API) lists all keys with status, role and validity.

usage.ui: Zscaler Admin Console > Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Private Access; filter Client ID; Download for CSV

log_sources.name: ZPA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Records admin and API actions; Client ID column; 6-month retention.

credential_id_fields.notes: API key's client ID that made changes

anomaly_cues: Changes by an unfamiliar Client ID

containment.steps: Disable or delete the ZPA API key.
containment.notes: Docs do not say whether issued tokens end before their validity interval (max 3,600 s).

calls.log_notes: ZPA audit action list includes Sign In
ZPA audit log documents changes and sign-ins, not reads

credentials.name: Sandbox API Token with ZIA admin credentials

authentication.summary: Sandbox Submission API uses an org API token plus ZIA admin username and password to create a session.

federation.details: Password-based; same Authentication Service restriction as zscaler-3.

renewal.summary: Reuse token and admin credentials to create a new session.

administration.summary: Up to 5 tokens per org; regenerate or delete from the Sandbox API Token page.

inventory.details: Sandbox API Token page (Administration > API > Internet & SaaS API > Sandbox API Token).

token_format.notes: Org-level sandbox token plus admin credentials.

log_sources.name: ZIA audit logs
log_sources.notes: Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Internet & SaaS; records Admin UI and API actions; 6-month retention; NSS admin audit feed.

lifecycle_events.notes: ZIA audit category/sub-category; exact token events not documented

containment.steps: Regenerate or delete the Sandbox API token.
containment.notes: Regeneration immediately invalidates the old token; effect on open sessions not stated.
